correctness.rationale: Recomputed the rotating-frame equation xdot=-beta(y-y_lag), ydot=beta(x-x_lag)+2(alpha-beta)x and F(lambda,k)=lambda²+beta²(1-exp(-lambda))²+beta*k*(1-exp(-lambda)). The lambda=0 root is simple for k>0 with derivative beta*k. At k=0, each factor lambda±i beta(1-e^-lambda) has no nonzero closed-right-half-plane root for beta<pi/2: imaginary crossing requires odd pi=2beta and no roots can arrive from infinity since |lambda|<=2beta; for small beta the integral h(lambda)=lambda int_0^1 e^-s lambda ds excludes them, and continuity completes the full beta interval. For k>0 the imaginary part at i omega equals beta sin omega[2beta(1-cos omega)+k], so nonzero imaginary roots require odd omega=(2j+1)pi and then k=((2j+1)^2 pi²-4beta²)/(2beta). Direct F_lambda at crossing = -((omega²+4beta²)/2)+2i omega; d lambda/d alpha has strictly positive real part. Right-half-plane roots obey |lambda|²<=4beta²+2beta*k and cannot appear from infinity on bounded k intervals; hence exact root count. The RFDE linearization principle gives attraction modulo S1, and positive eigenvalues instability, not Hopf branch type. Independent direct determinant and derivative substitutions tested beta pi/6, pi/3,1.3 with j=0..3; source script read, its finite Newton continuations are not proof.
